cases.description: Microsoft's documented example: 1 unit of principal compounded at 9%, 11% then 10%
cases.expected_note: Microsoft publishes this example (=FVSCHEDULE(1,{0.09,0.11,0.1})) with the result displayed as 1.3309. The documented computation -- principal times the product of (1+rate) over the schedule -- is exact here: 1 * 1.09 * 1.11 * 1.10 = 1.330890 with no rounding, so 1.33089 is asserted at 7 dp rather than the page's 4-dp display

cases.description: The schedule is applied multiplicatively to any principal
DIVERGENCE PROBE: Excel documents empty cells in the schedule as zeros (a 0% period), not as skipped
cases.expected_note: Verbatim from Microsoft: 'The values in schedule can be numbers or blank cells; any other value produces the #VALUE! error value for FVSCHEDULE. Blank cells are taken as zeros (no interest).' So the blank is a 0% period: 1000 * 1.1 * 1.0 * 1.1 = 1210. An engine that silently skipped the blank would get the same answer here, but an engine that errored on the blank would not -- so this pins the documented 'blank means 0%' rule

cases.description: A negative rate in the schedule shrinks the principal
Non-numeric values in the schedule are an error, not a zero
cases.expected_note: Verbatim from Microsoft: 'any other value produces the #VALUE! error value for FVSCHEDULE'. Note this is the opposite of most statistical functions, which ignore stray text in a reference, and it differs from an empty cell, which the same sentence documents as a zero rate
